subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 3: Grammar – may, might, could, can’t, must
outcomes: Know when to use must, can't and may/might/could.
Make deductions about animals from clues.
Give a reason for your deduction.

tf.s: We use must when we are sure something is true.
tf.why: Yes: It has a hump. It must be a camel.

tf.s: We use can't when we are sure something is not true.
tf.why: Yes: It doesn't have wings. It can't be a bird.

tf.s: May, might and could mean we are not sure.
tf.why: Yes, they show it is possible.

tf.s: “It can't to be a bear” is correct.
tf.why: After a modal, use the base verb: It can't be a bear.

tf.s: It has eight legs and makes webs. It must be a spider.
tf.why: Spiders have eight legs and make webs.

tf.s: It has flippers but no fins. It must be a fish.
tf.why: Fish have fins, so it can't be a fish.

tf.s: “It might be a cat” and “It must be a cat” mean the same.
It has antennae and six legs. It must be an insect.
tf.why: Insects have six legs and antennae.

tf.s: The light is off. They can't be at home. Here can't means we are sure they are not at home.
tf.why: Can't shows we are sure it is not true.

tf.s: Someone is at the door. We don't know who. “It must be Dad” is the best sentence.
tf.why: We are not sure, so we say It might be Dad.

boxes.q: It has a hump and lives in the desert. It ___ be a camel.
It doesn't have wings. It ___ be a bird.
boxes.why: We are sure it is not a bird.

boxes.q: I'm not sure what it is. It ___ be a fox.
boxes.why: Might shows we are not sure.

boxes.q: It has wings and a beak. It ___ be a bird.
boxes.why: Wings and a beak tell us it's a bird.

boxes.q: It isn't moving. It (must / can't) be asleep.
boxes.why: Not moving tells us it is asleep.

boxes.q: Her phone is ringing but she isn't answering. She ___ be busy.
boxes.why: We are quite sure she is busy.

boxes.q: Which modal means 100% sure it is true?
Which modal means 0% – sure it is not true?
It lays eggs, swims and has a beak like a duck. What must it be?
boxes.why: Only the platypus fits all three clues.

boxes.q: After must, can't or might, we use…
boxes.why: Example: It might be a cat.

hunt.q: Hump, desert: it must be a…
No wings: it ___ be a bird.

mcq.q: Which modal do we use when we are sure something is not true?
mcq.why: Can't = we are sure it is not true.

mcq.q: Which modal do we use when we are sure something is true?
Which group of modals means we are not sure?
Correct: It can't to be a bear.
o: It not can be a bear.

mcq.q: Make a deduction: It has eight legs and makes webs.
mcq.why: Eight legs and webs = a spider.

mcq.q: Make a deduction: It has antennae and six legs.
mcq.why: Insects have six legs and antennae.

mcq.q: There are big paw prints and long claw marks. Which deduction is best?
o: It might be a bear. It must be a big animal.
mcq.why: Big paws and claws mean a big animal.

mcq.q: What is the difference between It might be a cat and It must be a cat?
o: Might is for the past; must is for the future.
mcq.why: Modals show how sure we are.

mcq.q: Someone is at the door. Why is It might be Dad better than It must be Dad?
o: Because we are not sure who it is.
Because Dad is never at home.
Because might is the past tense.

mcq.q: A picture shows fur and claws. Which pair of deductions makes sense?
o: It might be a cat. It can't be a fish.
It must be a fish. It might be a bird.
It can't be a cat. It must be a snake.
It must be a bird. It can't be a cat.
mcq.why: Fish don't have fur, but cats do.
